forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Worcester Council behind on five audit recommendations on spending controls
news_drafts.lead: Worcester Council's Audit and Governance Committee was told the council has 19 outstanding internal audit recommendations, of which 5 are overdue. The overdue findings cover transparency code publication, reporting of purchasing card spending, and contract management monitoring. The council has implemented 74 per cent of recommendations overall, just below its 75 per cent target. The recommendations follow audits of the council's financial controls and procurement processes.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appx 1 Internal Audit Progress Report WCC

findings.headline: Worcester wrote off £60k of Council Tax debt and £91k of Business Rates debt in Q2 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper reports write-offs for the quarter, with the largest Council Tax category being insolvency (£41k across 17 accounts) and the largest Business Rates category also being insolvency (£91k across 10 accounts). Worcester's share of the write-offs is £6k of Council Tax and £37k of Business Rates.
findings.matters: Insolvency-driven write-offs at this scale are a measure of collection risk that finance officers at other councils compare when reviewing bad debt provisions.
findings.figures: £60k Council Tax written off (42 accounts); £91k Business Rates written off (12 accounts); Worcester share £6k and £37k
findings.quote: During the second quarter of 2026/27 £60k of Council Tax debt was written off along with £91k of Business Rates.

findings.headline: Worcester paid 94.3% of invoices within 30 days in Q2 2026/27, against a 100% target, and 84.6% of local supplier invoices within 10 days, against a 90% target.
findings.detail: The paper reports payment performance for the quarter. Both measures are below their stated targets.
findings.matters: Late payment performance against a local supplier target is an indicator finance directors and lenders use to judge a council's cash management and supplier relationships.
findings.figures: 94.3% of invoices paid within 30 days (target 100%); 84.6% of local supplier invoices paid within 10 days (target 90%)
findings.quote: For Q2 2026/27 performance was 94.3% paid on time.

findings.headline: Worcester forecasts planning fee and PCN income will generate a surplus of c£210k in 2026/27, after the planning fees budget was reduced in February 2026.
findings.detail: The paper says the planning fees budget was lowered at budget setting to reflect past performance, but income achieved in 2025/26 means an overall surplus of c£210k is now anticipated. Development management fees are forecast at £386k against a £172k budget.
findings.matters: Income running ahead of a reduced budget is a signal other councils will compare with their own planning fee budgeting.
findings.figures: c£210k planning income surplus; £386k development management forecast against £172k budget
findings.quote: an overall surplus of c£210k is anticipated.

findings.headline: Worcester's food waste vehicle order needs an additional £186,000, with delivery of the 7 vehicles moved to 2027/28.
findings.detail: The paper says larger food waste vehicles needed to be ordered at an extra cost of £186,000. This will be funded from a mix of revenue underspends and a review of the Fleet capital budget, which has created headroom and slippage into future years.
findings.matters: A cost increase on a fleet order, funded by reallocating underspends and slipping other fleet spend, is a pattern other councils facing vehicle price rises will recognise.
findings.quote: needed to be ordered at an additional cost of £186,000

findings.headline: Worcester's 2026/27 capital forecast is £21.086m against a revised budget of £27.371m, a variance of £6.285m.
findings.detail: The Appendix 4 total shows a forecast £6.285m below the revised budget. The paper says variances on the Towns Fund, Food Waste Collection and the Ops Vehicle Replacement reflect timing changes to be met from overall funding in future years.
findings.matters: Slippage of this size against the capital programme affects borrowing timing and is a point of comparison for other councils' capital delivery.
findings.figures: £27.371m revised budget; £21.086m forecast; £6.285m variance; £1.233m Towns Fund forecast against £5.291m budget
